## The Great Blue Hole: a flight over the reef or a deep dive

The Great Blue Hole lies in the Caribbean Sea within Lighthouse Reef Atoll, off the coast of [Belize](/belize/). This nearly circular marine sinkhole is about 300 m wide and more than 120 m deep. Its dark-blue center stands out against the turquoise shallows when viewed from above. Underwater, divers encounter steep limestone walls and ancient cave formations.

Protected as the Blue Hole Natural Monument, the site forms part of the Belize Barrier Reef Reserve System, inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 1996. Its significance lies in both its geology and the surrounding marine ecosystem. For visitors, the main practical choice is **to admire the shape of the Blue Hole on a scenic flight or travel there by boat for a dive**. These are very different experiences.

## What you see from an aircraft and underwater

| Experience | Main attraction |
|---|---|
| Scenic flight | The circular shape and contrast of colors |
| Scuba diving | Underwater walls and geological formations |
| Boat trip | The atoll, reefs and open sea |

**From the air**, it becomes clear why the Great Blue Hole is a symbol of Belize: an almost perfectly dark circle surrounded by shallow water and the reef formations extending across Lighthouse Reef. No diving qualifications are required for the flight. Departures do, however, depend on the weather, visibility and the operating airline.

**On a dive**, the aim is different: to see part of the deep underwater sinkhole and its limestone formations. This is not an ordinary shallow-water snorkeling trip over coral. The dive profile, qualification requirements and maximum depth are determined by the dive operator and each participant's training. Travelers should discuss their experience, certification, health and recent flights in advance. Even a certified diver may find a shallower reef dive more suitable.

**From a boat**, you can appreciate the surrounding atoll, but the sinkhole's geometry is less striking than from the air. A day trip to Lighthouse Reef involves time at sea and depends on wave conditions. If the famous circular view is your priority, a boat trip and a scenic flight are not equivalent.

## Where the Great Blue Hole is and how to include it in your trip

The Great Blue Hole is at Lighthouse Reef Atoll, far from the urban beaches. You cannot see it from the waterfront in [Belize City](/belize/place/belize-city/) or on a regular walk around [Ambergris Caye](/belize/place/ambergris-caye/). A dedicated air or sea excursion is required.

Ada Tours offers a [scenic flight over the Great Blue Hole in Belize](/belize/great-blue-hole/great-blue-hole-scenic-flight/). This is a sightseeing flight in a small aircraft shared with other travelers. Specific arrangements, departure times and the option to add it to your journey are agreed for your chosen itinerary.

For example, on the [“Guatemala, Honduras and Belize”](/multi-country/tour/guatemala-honduras-belize/) journey, time on Ambergris Caye follows visits to Central America's archaeological sites. A flight over the Blue Hole is offered **as an optional extra** on a free day. The distinction matters: the flight should not be assumed to be included automatically in every tour mentioning Belize.

If you want to see reef fish, rays and nurse sharks on comparatively shallow marine excursions, explore a different site, [Hol Chan Marine Reserve](/belize/place/hol-chan-marine-reserve/). It involves a different departure time, area and activity. You can compare these options with [diving as a travel interest](/interests/diving/) and the full [selection of Belize tours](/belize/tour/).

## When to plan a flight or sea excursion

Belize has a tropical climate, and sea conditions can differ from the weather over the mainland. Cloud cover, visibility and wind matter for scenic flights; boat trips also depend on wave height and sea conditions. A particular calendar month alone cannot guarantee an excursion will operate.

If the Great Blue Hole is the main reason for your trip, leave time for schedule changes and avoid placing the excursion immediately before an international flight. This flexibility is especially useful during tropical-storm season and the rainier months. Divers must also observe the recommended interval between diving and flying, following guidance from a qualified operator and relevant diving organization.

Check the rules for visiting this protected area. The underwater formations, corals and wildlife matter more than a dramatic photograph: do not touch natural features, leave litter or disregard the instructions of your licensed guide.

## Two Blue Holes in Belize: do not confuse them

Belize has another site with a similar name: [St. Herman's Blue Hole National Park](/belize/place/st-hermans-blue-hole-national-park/). There, Blue Hole means **a small freshwater pool in tropical forest**, close to limestone caves on the mainland. The circular marine sinkhole at Lighthouse Reef is much farther away, in the Caribbean Sea.

When choosing a trip, check the English name and type of excursion: Great Blue Hole and a scenic flight over the atoll are one option; St. Herman's Blue Hole and the forest pool are another. Both have separate pages in the [Belize places directory](/belize/place/).

## Frequently asked questions about the Great Blue Hole

### Can you see the Great Blue Hole without diving?

Yes. Its circular shape is clearly visible on a [scenic flight](/belize/great-blue-hole/great-blue-hole-scenic-flight/). Unlike a deep dive, a flight requires no scuba certification, but it depends on flying conditions and the carrier's operating requirements.

### Is diving in the Great Blue Hole suitable for beginners?

The deeper parts of the sinkhole require preparation and careful depth management. The operator decides whether a diver can participate based on certification, experience, health and the dive plan. For a first encounter with Belize's marine life, compare this option with shallower reef excursions.

### Are the Great Blue Hole and Hol Chan the same place?

No. The [Great Blue Hole](/belize/place/great-blue-hole/) is at Lighthouse Reef, while [Hol Chan](/belize/place/hol-chan-marine-reserve/) is a separate marine reserve near Ambergris Caye. The trips differ in location, duration and purpose.

### Is the flight included in the price of a Belize tour?

That depends on the particular program. On the [“Guatemala, Honduras and Belize”](/multi-country/tour/guatemala-honduras-belize/) itinerary mentioned above, the Blue Hole flight is an optional activity on a free day. Check the conditions and price in the specific offer rather than assuming the terms of one trip apply to another.

## The Great Blue Hole: an optional flight on a Belize itinerary

The [Great Blue Hole](/belize/place/great-blue-hole/) is near Lighthouse Reef Atoll off the coast of Belize. Its almost perfectly round dark center, surrounded by turquoise reef waters, is best viewed from the air. Several Ada Tours itineraries therefore offer it **as a separate scenic flight**, to be arranged in addition to the main tour.

This option suits travelers already planning time on Belize's Caribbean islands who want to see the famous natural landmark without turning their vacation into a dedicated diving expedition. See the [Great Blue Hole scenic flight](/belize/great-blue-hole/great-blue-hole-scenic-flight/) for details.

## Which tours offer the flight?

Optional visits differ fundamentally from the core itinerary: listing the Great Blue Hole among possible stops **does not in itself mean** that a flight has been paid for or will take place automatically.

| Itinerary | When to add the flight |
|---|---|
| [Guatemala, Honduras and Belize, 12 days](/multi-country/tour/guatemala-honduras-belize/) | A free day on Ambergris Caye, toward the end of the trip |
| [Belize in 6 days](/belize/tour/belize-wonders-6-days/) | An optional group flight while staying in San Pedro |
| [Cancún and Belize, 11 days](/multi-country/tour/cancun-belize-11-days/) | Before returning from Ambergris Caye to Belize City |
| [Wonders of Guatemala and Belize](/multi-country/tour/guatemala-belize-wonders/) | During the Caribbean section, before the final transfer |

These journeys have different priorities. The first focuses on Maya cities in 3 countries; the Mexico–Belize itinerary combines Yucatán archaeology with the Caribbean; and the short Belize trip combines western forests with time on [Ambergris Caye](/belize/place/ambergris-caye/). It makes sense to compare **the journeys themselves** first, then check whether there is a suitable free slot for the flight.

## Scenic flight, snorkeling or diving?

The Great Blue Hole is a deep underwater karst sinkhole. The view from a plane and the experience underwater serve different purposes.

**A scenic flight** offers the overhead view: a dark center, a pale ring of reef and the patterns of shallow seawater. This is the optional activity we offer with the listed Ada Tours itineraries. Flight duration and prices are detailed separately in the respective programs; some itineraries, for example, offer a group departure.

**Scuba diving** involves a boat trip to a remote atoll and a dive with breathing equipment. Experience, certification, health, weather and the dive operator's conditions are all important. An optional scenic flight does not mean scuba diving is included in the tour.

**Snorkeling** is different from deep diving too: watching the reef from the surface does not reveal its deep underwater geology. Travelers particularly interested in fish and coral should compare a separate outing to [Hol Chan Marine Reserve](/belize/place/hol-chan-marine-reserve/), which is closer to San Pedro.

## How to fit in an optional flight without rushing

The priority is to avoid missing part of the main itinerary. When a flight is scheduled before a transfer off the island or an international departure, check the time buffer, departure point, excursion duration and onward transport. Weather can disrupt small-aircraft flights, so a tight connection without extra time is inconvenient.

The [12-day journey through 3 countries](/multi-country/tour/guatemala-honduras-belize/) sets aside a free day for the Blue Hole. On the [Cancún–Belize tour](/multi-country/tour/cancun-belize-11-days/), the option falls on the day of travel from the island to Belize City. The second case requires particular attention to the order of activities and the water transfer.

Ada Tours helps coordinate the chosen option with the travel schedule: checking flight availability, payment conditions, departure point, weather and the time available before the next transfer. The final service arrangements depend on a confirmed optional booking.

## What to check before booking

- **Type of experience:** a scenic flight or a separate marine expedition. These are different products.
- **Day and departure:** whether the flight fits your night on Ambergris Caye and onward transfer.
- **Price:** the additional charge, currency, group or private flight conditions and any restrictions.
- **Weather:** what happens if the excursion is postponed or canceled.
- **Participation conditions:** small-aircraft baggage and weight limits, operator rules and arrangements for children.

For selecting the overall journey, browse the [Belize tours directory](/belize/tour/). If the Blue Hole itself is your main goal, start with the [specific scenic flight excursion](/belize/great-blue-hole/great-blue-hole-scenic-flight/) and then choose an itinerary with a suitable free day.

## Frequently asked questions about an optional visit to the Great Blue Hole

### Is the flight over the Great Blue Hole included in the tour price?

On these journeys, it is offered as an optional activity. What is included and the price depend on the chosen itinerary and flight option.

### Can you see the Blue Hole without diving?

Yes. A scenic flight lets you see it from above without scuba diving.

### Should I schedule the flight for departure day?

Only if the confirmed schedule leaves enough time before your transfer and flight. Weather and changes to small-aircraft schedules can disrupt a tight connection.

## Hidden Valley in Belize: forest trails, waterfalls and life in the Maya Mountains

[Hidden Valley](/belize/place/hidden-valley/) is in western Belize, in the Mountain Pine Ridge area of Cayo District. This privately protected natural area is associated with Hidden Valley Wilderness Lodge & Reserve. Pine-covered slopes meet broadleaf forest here, while small streams form waterfalls and natural pools.

**The main reason to stay in Hidden Valley is to spend time in the forest, rather than stop at a single viewpoint.** You can take a trail in the morning, relax during the day and save another walk for the following day. This experience is different from rushing from one tourist attraction to the next.

## How Hidden Valley differs from Mountain Pine Ridge Forest Reserve

Hidden Valley lies beside the government-managed [Mountain Pine Ridge Forest Reserve](/belize/place/mountain-pine-ridge-forest-reserve/). They are not the same place. Belize's Forest Department describes Hidden Valley separately as private land bordering the public forest reserve.

The Hidden Valley operator gives the area of its protected property as approximately 7,200 acres. It includes pine hills, rainforest, valleys, waterfalls and a network of trails. But **the presence of a natural attraction within a private reserve does not mean everyone has unrestricted access**. Access to certain waterfalls and walking routes may depend on staying at the lodge or arranging a guided excursion in advance.

The landscape here contrasts sharply with the familiar image of tropical Belize. Pine trees grow on sunlit slopes, while denser, humid greenery fills the valleys. Even a short walk can reveal several kinds of vegetation within a small area.

## Things to do in Hidden Valley

### Forest walks and viewpoints

The reserve has trails of varying lengths. For your first day, choose a walk that matches your fitness level and includes a viewpoint overlooking the forested valleys and mountain slopes. A longer hike calls for different arrangements for time, footwear and water.

Organized excursions and independent trails may have different rules. Ask whether a guide is needed, how you will get from your accommodation to the trailhead and whether the selected trail is accessible on your travel dates.

### Waterfalls and natural pools

The area is known for small woodland cascades and larger waterfalls. Among its natural attractions, the operator lists Butterfly Falls and King Vulture Falls. They lie in different parts of the property, and some areas have access restrictions.

Waterfalls look different after heavy rain, while slippery rocks and trails may require extra precautions. Swimming is permitted only where authorized and when conditions are suitable. Avoid packing several waterfall visits into one day without allowing for distances and climbs.

### Birds and wildlife

Different bird species inhabit the pine-covered slopes and moist forest. Hidden Valley reports hundreds of species recorded within the reserve, including the rare orange-breasted falcon. However, seeing a particular bird on a walk can never be guaranteed.

Binoculars, an early start and a companion familiar with local trails are useful for birdwatching. Travelers with this interest should compare [nature and wildlife tours in Belize](/interests/wildlife/tours/belize/) and what each excursion day includes.

## Getting there and how much time to allow

[San Ignacio](/belize/place/san-ignacio/) is a convenient starting point for journeys through western Belize. The onward road crosses mountainous terrain. The final sections can be remote and require careful planning, particularly after rain. Hidden Valley itself recommends arranging a transfer in advance with a driver familiar with the local roads.

If Hidden Valley is just a day stop, choose the exact walk and departure time in advance. **An overnight stay offers more flexibility:** go birdwatching in the morning, relax during the day and visit another natural attraction the next day.

| Option | Best suited to |
|---|---|
| Short stop | One arranged walk |
| Overnight stay | Unhurried forest time and relaxation |
| Several nights | Different trails and wildlife observations |
| Transit without a walk | The natural scenery remains only a passing view |

Accommodation and services within the reserve differ from a typical city hotel. Before selecting a tour, check which walks are included, whether a guide is provided and how much free time remains.

## Combining Hidden Valley with Guatemala and Belize's coast

On the [12-day “Guatemala and Belize: Into the Maya World” tour](/multi-country/tour/guatemala-belize-maya-world-12-days/), Hidden Valley falls between the archaeological part of the trip and the Caribbean coast. The itinerary includes crossing the border from Guatemala, traveling via San Ignacio, walking in the nature reserve and spending the night at Hidden Valley.

The following day is reserved for rest and optional activities before the journey continues toward the sea. The combination of historic Maya cities, forest and [Ambergris Caye](/belize/place/ambergris-caye/) offers three very different experiences. Optional activities should not be assumed to be paid for simply because they are available on the property.

Read about the walk on the [Hidden Valley nature walk excursion](/belize/hidden-valley/hidden-valley-nature-walk/) page. Check the details and conditions for any other activities.

{{#if catalog.hasTours}}
There are {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} associated with Hidden Valley. The details of your stay and access to private natural attractions depend on the selected program.
{{/if}}

## Frequently asked questions about Hidden Valley

### Are Hidden Valley and Mountain Pine Ridge the same place?

No. Hidden Valley is a private nature reserve bordering the [government-managed Mountain Pine Ridge Forest Reserve](/belize/place/mountain-pine-ridge-forest-reserve/). Their trail and waterfall access rules differ.

### Can you visit every waterfall without staying overnight?

You should not assume unrestricted access to all waterfalls. Some require an overnight stay or a prearranged excursion. Check the specific conditions with the operator organizing your visit.

### What should I bring for a walk in the reserve?

Comfortable closed-toe shoes, water, a small backpack, rain protection and insect repellent. Binoculars are useful for birdwatching. Confirm the trail's difficulty and any additional equipment before setting out.

### Is it worth combining Hidden Valley with western Belize and Tikal?

Yes, especially if your route already passes through [San Ignacio](/belize/place/san-ignacio/) after Guatemala's historic sites. Set aside time for the forest, allow for the border crossing and avoid turning the nature stop into a rushed transfer.

## Which tours visit Hidden Valley?

Here you can find {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} visiting [Hidden Valley](/belize/place/hidden-valley/) as part of the **main itinerary**, rather than as an optional activity. The confirmed route is [“Guatemala and Belize: The Maya World, Atitlán, Tikal and the Caribbean”](/multi-country/tour/guatemala-belize-maya-world-12-days/). This **12-day, 11-night** journey includes the forest stay halfway through its Belize section.

Hidden Valley is a stop between the cultural experiences in Guatemala and the island stay on [Ambergris Caye](/belize/place/ambergris-caye/). The itinerary reveals the changing landscapes of Central America: highland villages around a lake, archaeological sites in the lowlands of Petén, pine-covered hills and the Caribbean coast.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_guatemala_belize_maya_world_12_days}}

For details of the forests, trails and waterfalls, see the [Hidden Valley destination page](/belize/place/hidden-valley/). Here you can compare the **ready-made tour** day by day and review its confirmed inclusions.

## Days 8–10: how the reserve fits into the itinerary

| Day | Program |
|---|---|
| 8 | Travel from Guatemala and take a walk in the reserve |
| 9 | Free day at Hidden Valley |
| 10 | Travel toward the sea via Belize City |

**Day 8.** After breakfast, travelers leave Petén, cross the Guatemala–Belize border and continue via [San Ignacio](/belize/place/san-ignacio/) to Hidden Valley. **A walk in the nature reserve is included** in the confirmed tour services. The overnight stay is at Hidden Valley. A separate [Hidden Valley nature walk excursion](/belize/hidden-valley/hidden-valley-nature-walk/) page explains the natural highlights of this stop.

**Day 9.** The itinerary leaves a day free. You can relax at the hotel, choose one of the activities offered locally or consider an additional trip to the archaeological site of Caracol. **Caracol and the other optional excursions are not included in the basic services**. A free day should therefore not be mistaken for a prepaid package covering every route in the reserve. Another night is spent at Hidden Valley.

**Day 10.** The morning begins with a transfer from Belize's forested interior to [Belize City](/belize/place/belize-city/). A water transfer then takes travelers to Ambergris Caye, with accommodation on the Caribbean coast. From this point, the itinerary turns to seaside relaxation.

The complete tour includes **2 nights** at Hidden Valley. This makes a real difference compared with a trip that offers only a brief stop in the natural area between transfers.

## Why spend 2 nights at Hidden Valley?

The reserve is in the [Mountain Pine Ridge](/belize/place/mountain-pine-ridge-forest-reserve/) area of western Belize. Caribbean pine, patches of tropical broadleaf forest, rivers, waterfalls and viewpoints can all be found here. Hidden Valley Wilderness Lodge operates a network of walking trails within its private nature reserve, which its management describes as part of its own protected property.

For travelers, two nights primarily offer **the chance to separate the included walk from free time**. The day of the border crossing includes an organized nature stop. The following day, you can set your own pace: join an optional excursion, walk an agreed trail or stay at the lodge. Access to particular paths and waterfalls depends on local conditions, permissions and the type of guiding selected.

The scenery differs from the humid lowland jungle surrounding [Tikal and Flores](/guatemala/place/tikal-and-flores/). It is a good option for travelers who want to complement Maya ruins and Central American islands with an experience of **forested mountains**.

## What comes before and after Hidden Valley?

The itinerary follows a natural progression between regions, so visiting Hidden Valley does not require returning to the capital or crossing the border a second time.

- **Guatemalan Highlands:** Chichicastenango Market, Maya villages around [Lake Atitlán](/guatemala/place/lake-atitlan/), the Iximché archaeological site and [Antigua Guatemala](/guatemala/place/antigua-guatemala/).
- **Petén Lowlands:** a guided visit to [Tikal and Flores](/guatemala/place/tikal-and-flores/), followed by overland travel to Belize.
- **Western Belize:** [San Ignacio](/belize/place/san-ignacio/) and Hidden Valley, with an organized nature walk and a free day.
- **Caribbean Sea:** [Ambergris Caye](/belize/place/ambergris-caye/), where the journey ends with beach time.

The transition from temples to mountains and then an island particularly suits travelers hoping to see **both countries on one trip**. If your priority is several days of dedicated trekking, consider the time allocated to the reserve: this tour offers 2 nights, not an extended walking expedition.

## Group or private format

The [12-day itinerary](/multi-country/tour/guatemala-belize-maya-world-12-days/) offers group and private options for 2027. Group departures are listed for Saturdays; private departures operate daily under the program's specified conditions. Group arrangements are stated for **2–16 participants**, with Spanish- and Italian-speaking guides. A Russian-speaking guide should not be assumed.

In both formats, Hidden Valley remains the forest stop between Guatemala and the island. However, a private guide, extra routes, language assistance on a particular walk and inclusion of a Caracol excursion depend on the **selected fare**. Listing activities available at the reserve does not mean they are all included in the price.

When comparing options, pay attention to the actual number of nights, border-crossing arrangements, domestic flights and excluded excursions. The source itinerary describes flight surcharges and accommodation arrangements separately; the confirmed current prices and options are presented on the [tour's own page](/multi-country/tour/guatemala-belize-maya-world-12-days/).

## When to choose a Hidden Valley route and when to choose another Belize tour

The Hidden Valley route combines **Guatemala's culture, Belize's forests and an island stay**. It particularly appeals to travelers who want to see Atitlán and Tikal while making time for nature.

If caves and water-based adventures are your priority, compare it with [“Belize: Mainland / Island Adventure”](/belize/tour/belize-mainland-island-adventure/). Its main itinerary includes [Jaguar Paw](/belize/place/jaguar-paw/) and cave tubing. This is **a different nature activity**: floating through a cave river on inflatable tubes rather than walking through the forests of Hidden Valley.

If marine excursions are your main goal, take a closer look at [tours through Hol Chan](/belize/place/hol-chan-marine-reserve/tour/) and [all Belize tours](/belize/tour/). They vary not only in places visited but also in days spent on the mainland, which boat trips are offered and what the chosen package actually includes.

For other natural experiences in Belize, explore [nature-focused journeys across the country](/interests/wildlife/tours/belize/). These thematic selections may feature different landscapes and trip durations.

## Practical questions before traveling

### Is Hidden Valley included in the itinerary or optional?

On the 12-day tour described above, Hidden Valley is part of the **main itinerary**: the organized walk is scheduled for day 8, and overnight stays follow days 8 and 9. Optional free-day excursions are a separate choice.

### How long do travelers spend in the reserve?

The itinerary provides for arrival on day 8, a free day on day 9 and departure on the morning of day 10. It does not specify an exact number of hours on each trail.

### Can I visit Caracol during the stay?

Caracol is listed for day 9 as **a possible optional excursion**. It is not a mandatory included activity and must be arranged separately.

### Does the trip include the sea?

Yes. After the nature portion, the journey continues to [Ambergris Caye](/belize/place/ambergris-caye/). This is a separate island segment, not a continuation of the reserve's forest walks.

### Is this route suitable if I only want to visit Hidden Valley?

This is primarily **a combined Guatemala and Belize journey**. If you want a complete vacation devoted to trails, waterfalls and birdwatching in the reserve, 2 nights may be too short. Discuss such a request as a different itinerary rather than assuming the existing tour includes additional time.

## Hol Chan in Belize: snorkeling along the coral reef

**Hol Chan Marine Reserve lies near [Ambergris Caye](/belize/place/ambergris-caye/), not far from San Pedro in [Belize](/belize/).** This protected section of the Belize Barrier Reef includes coral communities, seagrass beds and mangrove habitats. The name Hol Chan is translated as “little channel”: a natural opening in the reef allows marine animals to move between parts of the waterway.

The reserve was established in 1987 and subsequently expanded. Conservation restrictions coexist with regulated boat excursions. Visitors primarily come to observe life underwater: colorful fish can be seen along the reef and, with luck, turtles and rays. Sightings depend on sea conditions and chance, so no particular species can be guaranteed.

## Hol Chan and Shark Ray Alley: two distinct zones

The names **Hol Chan** and **Shark Ray Alley** often appear together in excursion descriptions, but they refer to different parts of the protected marine area. It helps to understand the distinction before choosing a boat trip.

| Area | What you may see |
|---|---|
| **Hol Chan Channel, Zone A** | Reef fish, coral ecosystems and the channel through the reef |
| **Shark Ray Alley, Zone D** | Nurse sharks and rays in shallower water |
| **Other reserve zones** | Seagrass, mangroves and other protected habitats |

Zone A covers sections of the reef and its natural channel. Schools of fish are particularly interesting here, and the underwater terrain makes for memorable swimming. Shark Ray Alley lies farther south and is known for encounters with nurse sharks and southern stingrays. These animals move freely through the sea. A stop named on an itinerary confirms the area to be visited, not an encounter at any particular distance.

When selecting an excursion, check whether the boat visits both zones or makes only one stop. Swim time, water conditions and group arrangements may differ.

## How snorkeling works and who it suits

Boats usually depart from San Pedro on Ambergris Caye. On arrival, the guide explains how to enter the water, which way to swim and the conservation restrictions. To observe marine life near the surface, participants use a mask, snorkel and fins; a suitable life jacket is useful for anyone less confident in open water.

**The main practical considerations are currents and sea conditions on the day.** Water movement may be noticeable in the reef channel, while visibility and swimming comfort vary. Tell the guide about your swimming experience, health and any limitations before departure. For children, check minimum age, required swimming ability and the particular boat excursion's conditions.

Surface snorkeling and **scuba diving** require different training. The reserve management permits scuba diving with appropriate certification or as part of instructor-led training. Scuba diving is prohibited in the exclusive recreational zone at Shark Ray Alley, where visits are for observation from the surface. Rules for each zone always take precedence over general promotional descriptions.

## Protecting coral and marine animals

Hol Chan is protected to conserve a living ecosystem. On excursions, collecting coral, shells or other natural objects, chasing animals or damaging the reef with fins is prohibited. Use designated areas and follow your guide's instructions.

Fishing and feeding fish are restricted in the reef-channel zone. Shark Ray Alley's rules differ in some details, but they do not permit visitors to touch or feed sharks and rays on their own. The best way to observe underwater life is to keep a safe distance, stay with the group and avoid touching the seabed or coral.

## Which Ada Tours itineraries include Hol Chan?

On the [“Belize: San Pedro and Ambergris Caye”](/belize/tour/belize-san-pedro-ambergris-caye/) trip, day 2 features **a half-day snorkeling excursion to Hol Chan and Shark Ray Alley**. That tour includes entrance fees, snorkeling gear and local guide services for the excursion. These terms apply to the named tour.

On the [“Exploring Belize”](/belize/tour/explore-belize/) itinerary, the reserve is visited during the marine section of the trip, with a snorkeling stop. In [“Best of Belize”](/belize/tour/best-of-belize/), trips to Hol Chan and Shark Ray Alley appear among the **optional paid activities** for a free day on the island. Before booking, compare not just whether “Hol Chan” appears in the description, but whether boat transport, equipment, fees and transfers are included in that particular program.

Travelers interested in wildlife can also browse [other nature and wildlife tours](/interests/wildlife/). Snorkeling in the sea and a dedicated scuba diving program are, however, different activities with different conditions.

## When to plan a boat trip

Belize's Caribbean coast is warm year-round, but weather and water conditions vary. Waves, wind and visibility can affect the route and whether swimming is possible in a particular zone. If your trip includes several marine activities, leave extra time and coordinate departures with current conditions.

Useful personal items include sun protection, a towel and suitable clothes for the boat. Check the selected tour description for equipment, life jackets and participation requirements. If you plan to scuba dive, confirm certification and the requirements of the specific diving program as well.

## Frequently asked questions about Hol Chan

### Where is Hol Chan Marine Reserve?

It lies off the southern part of [Ambergris Caye](/belize/place/ambergris-caye/), close to San Pedro. Snorkeling sites are reached by boat.

### Can you see sharks and rays?

Yes. Shark Ray Alley is known for sightings of nurse sharks and rays. These are wild animals, however, and sightings are not guaranteed. Follow the rules and do not attempt to touch them.

### Do I need scuba certification to snorkel?

No scuba certification is needed for ordinary snorkeling with a mask and snorkel. Scuba diving has separate reserve requirements depending on certification and the form of instruction.

### Do all Ambergris Caye tours include Hol Chan?

No. The [San Pedro itinerary](/belize/tour/belize-san-pedro-ambergris-caye/) includes the visit, while [“Best of Belize”](/belize/tour/best-of-belize/) offers it as an optional activity. Check the conditions of the specific itinerary.
